scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You finish one video, and YouTube lines up the next one you'll probably click. How does it choose from billions?

scenes.name: candidates
scenes.text: First, a fast system picks a few hundred possible videos for you, out of billions, based on what you and similar viewers watch.

scenes.name: signals
scenes.text: It looks at your watch history, searches, likes, subscriptions, and what you skip or mark not interested.

scenes.name: rank
scenes.text: A second model scores each candidate, predicting how likely you are to click, and how long you'll actually keep watching.

scenes.name: satisfy
scenes.text: YouTube says it also uses surveys asking viewers if a video was worth their time, so it's not just about clicks.

scenes.name: mix
scenes.text: It adds some variety and fresh topics, so your feed doesn't become the same thing over and over.

scenes.name: control
scenes.text: You can steer it. Tap not interested, remove videos from history, or pause your watch history.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Narrow, score, satisfy, mix. Your next video, picked for you. Follow for more on how things really work.
